label: High when observer believes S2 is good and last choice was a2; low after unrewarded a1.
explanation: The raw candidate value of unit 5 is an anti-S1 belief signal: it decreases with the ideal observer log-odds that S1 is good (saturating, tanh(belief_lo)) on every phase, is higher after a previous a2 choice, and drops sharply after an unrewarded a1 trial (strongest at D1, around -1 relative to timing). Reward alone after a2 matters little. The free fit adds phase-specific belief and prev-action weights and the just-made a2 choice at D2 (+0.04 dev R2). Using the upcoming choice (future at D1/GO) would add more (0.82 dev), consistent with the unit tracking the a2-vs-a1 preference, but it is not recorded.

issues: The explanation says 'whether an a2 trial was rewarded matters little'. That is false at D1. Residual after timing at D1 is a2 S2 r +0.595 vs a2 S2 u -0.109, and a2 S1 r +0.564 vs a2 S1 u +0.325. At D1 the previous reward raises the unit whatever the previous choice was. Misses on the recorded short form put the largest systematic errors in D1 split by reward: under-predicted after a1 S1 r (+0.36) and a2 S1 r (+0.34), over-predicted after a2 S1 u (-0.36), a1 S1 u (-0.34) and a2 S2 u (-0.27).

At GO and D2 the reward effect is different: after a2 S1 u the unit is higher than after a2 S1 r (+0.66 vs +0.37 at GO). So 'low after unrewarded a1' plus a single reward-free a2 term hides a phase-dependent reward effect: at D1 reward raises the unit for both choices, while later phases follow the belief.

Swapping the third term for a D1-only reward-sign term gives test R^2 0.725, about the same as the a1-unrewarded term (0.719). Packing the two history effects into one term and adding the D1 reward-sign term raises test to 0.761.
Tanh saturation: tanh(belief_lo/2) scores better than tanh(belief_lo) (test 0.725 vs 0.719), so the belief dependence is softer than recorded.

The recorded form's numbers reproduce (test 0.7185; weights -0.48, +0.23, -0.53), and dropping the a1-unrewarded term costs 0.06 (0.657), so the core claims hold. The worst misses are windows where the unit is strongly negative while the ideal observer favours S2 (predicted +0.6 to +1.0). There the unit follows the agent's own a1 preference, not the observer, which is why the policy-decile reference scores 0.83. A gap of about 0.12 to the 'all observed' ceiling of 0.88 remains.
